newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index ends sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index ends sharply lower.

text.p: The Philippine stock market's main index fell sharply at close in heavy volume on Monday as an early bout of profit-taking in selected property issues trigerred across-the-board selling.
The main index fell 73.08 points lower, or 2.54 percent, at 2,808.65 points.
"There was profit-taking in most issues. Once they broke support, they started falling down with the same speed," said Juanis Barredo, analyst at Citisecurities Inc.
"This is partly profit-taking and partly a reaction to higher interest rates," said Minda Olonan, research head at HSBC James Capel Securities.
Turnover was heavy at 2.5 billion pesos with 88 decliners against 31 gainers. All sectors fell.

"A lot of foreigners were selling and these are basically the same people who couldn't get out when the market was so bad and are now grabbing the opportunity after last week's sharp gains," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor Hagedorn Securities.
Some of the index-linked issues that fell were Ayala Land Inc, Metro Pacific Corp, PLDT and Meralco.
Bucking the general trend was Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc which posted gains as investors felt earlier rumours about the firm being in a financial crisis were untrue, brokers said.
Megaworld, the most actively traded issue for the day, closed 55 centavos higher at 4.10 pesos.
Petron Corp shed 50 centavos to 6.90 pesos in late trade on news of an explosion in its refinery near Manila, Asia Pacific Capital analyst Carl Valentin said.
Citisecurities' Barredo said if the index persisted in its drop, but with lower volumes on Tuesday, the market may recover with hefty gains by the latter part of the week.
The support was pegged at 2,800 points.
